candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — cultural practices/beliefs and end-of-life care
candidate.educational_objective: Provide culturally responsive grief and end-of-life care by assessing client/family preferences and incorporating their cultural practices and beliefs when safely feasible.

options.A: Ask about the family's preferences and incorporate their cultural practices into care when they can be safely accommodated
options.B: Use the same mourning expectations for every family so care remains standardized
options.C: Discourage cultural rituals because grief should be expressed privately outside the health care setting
options.D: Use the nurse's own beliefs to determine which mourning practices are appropriate

candidate.rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan includes incorporating the client's cultural practices and beliefs when planning and providing care and providing end-of-life care and education. Therefore the nurse should assess the family's preferences and respectfully incorporate their practices when safe and feasible. B, C, and D impose standardized or nurse-centered expectations rather than individualized culturally responsive care.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Entry-level RN psychosocial care includes incorporating client cultural practices and beliefs into care and providing end-of-life care and education.
candidate.source_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10 / PDF p.14: incorporate client cultural practices and beliefs when planning and providing care; provide end-of-life care and education to clients
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A grieving family describes cultural practices they would like to follow after a client's death. Which nursing response is most appropriate?
